p.n: 지배되다 just states the fact; 당하다 stresses that the country suffered under the rule.

지배되다.h: be controlled or dominated, neutral passive

p.n: 지배당하다 adds a feeling of being a victim; 지배되다 is neutral.

통치되다.h: governed by a king or state, formal

p.n: 통치되다 means being governed by a ruler or government; 지배되다 is broader and means being controlled or dominated.

철수시키다.h: make or order others to pull out

p.n: 철수하다 means the subject itself leaves, so it is not natural with 직원들을 as the object.
체포되다 just reports the arrest, without stressing unfairness.

후퇴시키다.h: make someone or something pull back

p.n: 후퇴하다 does not take an object like 군인들을, so it cannot replace 후퇴시키다 here.

폐쇄시키다.h: force or order something to be shut down

p.n: 폐쇄하다 simply says it was closed, without the causative feeling.

기여하다.h: contribute; neutral, most common everyday choice

p.n: 공헌 sounds more like recognized merit.
Nearly the same; 흰색 is the standard dictionary form.

하양.h: bare color name, like in a rainbow list

p.n: Same meaning; 하양 is the color-list style name.

향상시키다.h: raise skill or quality; takes an object

p.n: 향상 raises the level; 개선 fixes problems.

향상되다.h: skill or level gets raised; passive form

p.n: 좋아졌어요 is casual; 향상되다 is more formal.

호전하다.h: same sense as passive, rarer active form

p.n: 호전되다 is the more usual form.
확대 does not fit physically widening a road.

멤버.h: casual loanword; member of team or band

p.n: 구성원 is more formal; 멤버 is casual.

대원.h: member of a squad, such as rescue

p.n: 대원 is mostly used for squads and corps; the others sound odd here.

일원.h: one person among a larger group

p.n: 일원 stresses being one of the group; 구성원 stresses making up the group.

조합원.h: member of a union or cooperative

p.n: 회원 is a general member; 조합원 specifically belongs to a union or cooperative.

들뜨다.h: giddy and unsettled, cannot calm down

p.n: 들뜨다 is a restless, floating mood; 흥분되다 is thrill.

희생시키다.h: sacrifice someone else; make them a victim

p.n: 희생하다 needs the actor to give up themselves; 희생시키다 sacrifices others.

하.h: lowest rank on a top-middle-low scale

p.n: 밑 means physical underside, not a low rank, so it cannot replace 하 in a class level.

고되다.h: tiring because of heavy work or effort

p.n: 지난하다 describes difficult processes, not being worn out by work, so it sounds unnatural here.

분야.h: area of study or work; abstract domain

p.n: 필드 is a physical sports ground, so it does not fit a field of work here.

들.h: open countryside plain; short native word

p.n: 밭 means a cultivated plot, while 들 is wild open land.

아아.h: drawn-out ah; stronger feeling or sigh

p.n: 아 is a lighter, quicker reaction with less emotion.

그 후.h: short form without a time particle

p.n: No real difference in meaning; 그 후에 adds the particle and sounds slightly fuller.

그 후에.h: fuller form with a time particle attached

p.n: Same meaning; 그 후 is a little more compact.

우아.h: more excited, playful wow of delight

p.n: 와 is the neutral, more common wow with less exuberance.
꼼짝 아니하다 is a stiff written form and does not fit the polite spoken ending.

꼼짝 아니하다.h: stiff written style; not stirring at all

p.o: 그는 꿈쩍 안 하고 앉아 있었다.
p.n: Same meaning; 꿈쩍 안 하다 is more colloquial and suggests a bigger movement.

껴안다.h: wrap both arms tightly around someone

p.n: 껴안다 is wrapping the arms around; 끌어안다 adds pulling the person close to your chest.

끌어안다.h: pull someone close against one's chest

p.n: 끌어안다 stresses pulling the child in close; 안다 only says you held the child.

공여하다.h: formal; grant funds or aid to others

p.n: 공여하다 is a formal written word for official aid; 주다 is plain and conversational.

아가리.h: rude for people; big animal mouth

p.n: 아가리 sounds cruder or wilder; 입 is neutral.

여성.h: neutral word for woman; humans only

p.n: 여류 sounds a bit dated and singles out a woman in a field; 여성 is neutral.

여.h: female as in 'male and ___'; fixed pairs

p.n: 여 is used in fixed pairs like 남과 여 and cannot be swapped alone for 여성.
여성 is only for human women, so it is not natural for a cat.

여류.h: woman in a profession; slightly dated

p.n: 여성 is the neutral modern choice; 여류 feels old-fashioned.
작다 is a neutral size; 조그맣다 adds a small, cute feel.

조그마하다.h: longer variant of the short-form synonym

p.n: Same meaning; 조그마하다 is just the longer form of 조그맣다.
잘다 suits small grains or fine pieces; 작다 is a general size.

수납하다.h: formal; collect fees paid to you

p.n: 수납하다 is formal cashier-side collection; 받다 is everyday.

사상.h: ideology; system of thought of a person or era

p.n: 사상 means his philosophy or ideology; 생각 means what he is thinking or his opinion.

결핍하다.h: short of something needed, e.g. nutrients

p.n: 결여 is about a missing quality or element, so it sounds odd with vitamins.
결여되다 is passive, so the particle changes to 이/가. The meaning is almost the same.
다른 생각 just means a different thought. 딴 생각 means your mind wandered off-topic.
다름 아니라 sounds a little more formal and polite.

다름 아니라.h: more formal opener giving the reason

p.s: 다름 아니라 오늘 회의 때문에 연락드렸습니다.
p.o: 다른 게 아니라 오늘 회의 때문에 연락드렸습니다.
p.n: The meaning is the same, but 다른 게 아니라 feels less formal.

부녀자.h: formal; women as a group, married

p.s: 이 길은 부녀자가 밤에 다니기 위험하다.
p.o: 이 길은 여자가 밤에 다니기 위험하다.
p.n: 여자 is plain and everyday. 부녀자 is a formal word for women as a group, mostly in notices and news.

씌우다.h: put something on someone else's head

p.n: 뒤집어쓰다 is for wearing something yourself. Using it here would need a different subject and sentence.

뒤집어쓰다.h: pull over whole head or body

p.n: 씌우다 means putting something on another person, so it cannot replace this self-action sentence.

신.h: short form, used with the verb for wearing

p.n: Same meaning. 신발 is the more common everyday word, while 신 sounds shorter and a bit more set-phrase-like.
휴일 sounds a bit more formal, like an official day off.

사랑하다.h: general word for love, strong emotion

p.n: 친애하다 is formal and used for greetings, so it does not fit a simple statement about family.

친애하다.h: formal affection, used in letter greetings

p.n: 사랑하는 is warmer and more emotional. 친애하는 is a formal, respectful way to say dear.

삼다.h: regard someone as a role or position

p.n: 만들다 would mean creating a friend. 삼다 means to treat or take someone as a friend.

사용하다.h: general word for using tools or things

p.n: 이용하다 sounds like using a shared or public facility. 사용하다 is plain use of a thing.

써먹다.h: casual: put knowledge or skills to use

p.n: 사용하다 is neutral and formal. 써먹다 is casual and stresses getting practical use out of something.

밧줄.h: thick heavy rope for ships, hauling

p.n: 줄 is vaguer and could be a thin string; 밧줄 clearly means a strong rope.

집다.h: pick up with fingers, chopsticks, or tongs

p.n: 줍다 cannot be used for grasping with chopsticks or tools.
남자 only states that he is male; 사나이 praises his manliness and courage.

오늘날.h: the present era, not this day

p.n: 오늘 means this day and cannot mean the present era.
이런 is neutral; 이따위 shows anger or disdain toward the words.

묘하다.h: subtly odd, hard to describe, intriguing

p.n: 이상하다 suggests something is wrong; 묘하다 is a complex feeling that is hard to name.
희한하다 shows surprise at something rare and amazing; 이상하다 just says it is odd.

곽.h: small paper box: tissues, cigarettes, matches

p.n: 상자 is a general box; 곽 is a small paper box such as a tissue or cigarette box.
상자 sounds a bit more standard; 박스 is casual and often means a cardboard box.

함.h: box for a use: mailbox, ballot, gifts

p.n: 함 forms fixed compounds like 우편함; 우편상자 is not used.
매달다 takes an object (hang something), but 매달리다 describes something already hanging.

구하다.h: seek to obtain something needed; jobs, rooms

p.n: 찾다 is the general word for searching; 구하다 stresses wanting to obtain it.

명칭.h: Formal name of things, never for people

p.n: 이름 is the everyday word and also works for people.

동무.h: Childhood playmate; comrade in North Korea

p.n: 친구 is neutral; 동무 feels old-fashioned and warm, or North Korean.

벗.h: Literary, old-fashioned word for a friend

p.n: 벗 sounds poetic and bookish; 친구 is the normal word.
끝장 is stronger and more dramatic, meaning finished or ruined.

종료.h: Formal end of an event or process

p.n: 종식 stresses the definitive end of something bad; 종료 is a neutral stop.
종료 means 'termination' and cannot replace 종국에는, which means 'in the end'.

말기.h: Last stage of an era or illness

p.n: 종말 means final destruction and does not describe an illness stage.

권장하다.h: officially encourage as desirable; policy, guidelines

p.n: 권고하다 is a stronger, more direct urging; 권장하다 encourages something as good practice.
정면 is the main face a viewer looks at; 앞면 just means the front side.

그리하다.h: formal or literary way to say 'do so'

p.n: 그리하다 sounds more formal or stiff.
마음 cannot replace 내심 as an adverb here; 마음속으로 would be needed.
Same meaning; 뜨이다 is less common and more literary.

뜨이다.h: catch the eye; literary; eyes opening

p.n: Same meaning; 띄다 is the more common form.

해양.h: oceans as a domain; marine, maritime

p.n: 대양 names a vast ocean itself and is not used as a modifier like this.

대양.h: one of the world's major oceans

p.n: 해양 refers to the marine realm in general, so crossing it sounds unnatural.

스토리.h: loanword; plot or storyline of a work

p.n: 이야기 is broader and softer; 스토리 stresses plot construction.
이유 is neutral; 사유 fits official forms.

사리.h: sense or logic in judging matters

p.n: 이치 refers to the underlying principle rather than judgment.
감사 is the common word; 사의 is formal and written.
라인 is a loanword and sounds more like a design or styling line; 선 is the general word.
Same meaning, but 밤 is more casual and everyday.

특수.h: special in kind; specialized, not general

p.n: 특별 부대 is not a natural phrase. 특수 marks a fixed, specialized category; 특별 means exceptional or out of the ordinary.

특별.h: special as in exceptional, out of ordinary

p.n: 특수한 날 sounds odd. 특별 means a day that stands out, while 특수 means a day of a specialized kind.
동참하다 sounds like joining in a shared effort that others already started; 참여하다 just says you take part.
방식 is more formal and sounds like a system or procedure; 식 is a casual 'manner' used mostly after 이런/그런/저런.

회합하다.h: assemble as a group; formal gathering

p.n: 회동하다 is for a few key people meeting, often officials; 회합하다 is for a group gathering formally.
보내다 is casual and general; 발송하다 is formal and used for mail, packages, and documents.

회부하다.h: refer a matter to a committee or court

p.n: 송치하다 is only for police sending a suspect or case to the prosecutors. 회부하다 refers any matter to a body.

호실.h: numbered room in hospital or hotel

p.n: 방 does not take a number this way; you would say 1705호 방 instead.

깎다.h: peel thinly with a knife; trim

p.n: Apples are peeled with a knife, so 까다 is not natural here.

까다.h: peel off shell or skin by hand

p.n: You do not cut a tangerine's peel off with a knife, so 깎다 is not natural.
교묘한 hints at trickery; 명석한 sounds like a smart, clear method.

총재.h: head of a bank or party

p.n: 총재 leads a bank or party; 회장 leads a club or company.

참석하다.h: be present at an event or meeting

p.n: 출석하다 is for classes or roll call, not a wedding.
Same meaning; 조금 is the neutral standard form.

도회.h: literary, old-fashioned word for a city

p.n: Same meaning; 도시 is the modern, everyday word.
술집 is a plain, everyday pub.

주점.h: formal, written word for a drinking place

p.n: Same meaning; 술집 is the everyday spoken word.

외관.h: outer look, mostly of buildings or objects

p.n: 외양 is possible but less typical for buildings.

외양.h: outward look, also of a person

p.n: 외관 sounds odd for a person; it fits buildings and objects.

등장.h: someone or something entering the scene

p.n: 출현 is for things or creatures emerging, so it sounds odd for a main character.
Same meaning; 등장 sounds more like entering a story or scene.
Same meaning; 피 sounds more casual.
Same meaning; 피어나다 feels more gradual and vivid.

피어나다.h: bloom gradually; feelings can emerge too

p.n: Same meaning; 피다 is the plain basic word.

힘.h: physical power or energy; basic word

p.n: The other word means a strong point or advantage, not physical power.

강세.h: upward market trend; also stress in speech

p.n: The other word means a personal or company strong point, not a market trend.

곡.h: a tune or piece; counts songs

p.n: The swap suggests a song with singing or lyrics rather than just the piece of music.

육체.h: physical body as opposed to mind or spirit

p.n: The swap is neutral; the original contrasts body with mind.

포괄되다.h: covered within a broad scope or umbrella

p.n: The swap simply says included; the original stresses a wide coverage.

집필.h: formal; act of writing a book or article

p.n: The swap sounds more scholarly and less like the process of writing a manuscript.

묘사하다.h: paint a vivid picture with words or art

p.n: The swap sounds like stating or narrating, with less of a vivid picture.

형용하다.h: express in words; mostly used negatively

p.s: 그 기쁨은 말로 형용할 수 없어요.
p.o: 그 기쁨은 말로 묘사할 수 없어요.
p.n: The swap is correct but means unable to portray in detail, while the original means unable to put into words.

최후.h: the very end; one's final moment

p.n: The swap is correct but plainer; the original suggests a downfall or death.

단대.h: short for a college within a university

p.n: With 대학 the student council belongs to the whole university, not one faculty.

집어넣다.h: stuff in quickly with the hand

p.n: 넣다 is neutral; 집어넣다 stresses a quick, casual push.
With 여러분 the claim is only about the people being addressed, not all people.

회담.h: formal talks between officials or leaders

p.n: 대담 would mean a public conversation like an interview, not negotiations or a summit.

역사.h: general word for the past; everyday

p.n: 청사 is literary and does not take 'learn a country's history' naturally.

청사.h: literary; records of history, set phrases

p.n: 역사 is the plain, neutral word; 청사 sounds literary and solemn.
Same meaning; 사학 is the shorter form, 역사학 the full standard name.
양해 sounds like asking to be excused or permitted, not to be understood emotionally.

가격하다.h: formal; a blow, news or boxing

강타하다.h: hit hard; storms, disasters, big impact

p.n: 때리다 sounds like a person hitting; it does not fit a storm well here.

때리다.h: everyday hit or beat, by a person

p.n: 가격하다 makes it formal and written, like a report of a blow.

미역.h: brown seaweed; soup and side dishes

p.n: 김 is already dried sheets; you do not soak it to rehydrate.

흥겹다.h: merry; lively, excited by music or festival

p.n: 행복하다 cannot describe music; it does not express a lively festive mood.

단란하다.h: harmonious and warm, mainly about family

p.n: 행복하다 is a general feeling; 단란하다 describes closeness and harmony.
거절하다 is a plain 'turn down'; 거부하다 is firmer, refusing outright.

거절하다.h: turn down a request or invitation

p.n: 거부하다 sounds harsher and more final than a simple turn-down.

연기자.h: performer; used for TV, broader sense

p.n: Both are natural; 배우 is the more common everyday word.
